actions.action: Gently hand-pull the seedlings and weeds (stowaways) from the pot
Take detailed leaf and flower photos and ask a plant ID subreddit to confirm the species
Check roots for circling, root-bound growth or waterlogging
If needed, repot into fresh well-draining mix (cactus mix with perlite, or a more moisture-retentive blend if not a succulent) in a pot with a drainage hole
Check that the top inch of soil is dry before watering
Acclimate the plant gradually to brighter light if it was recently moved
If yellowing spreads or spots, residue or webbing appear, post close-up photos of the affected leaves and undersides

reason: The answer mentions nutrient stress only as one possible cause of the yellowing and correctly flags the stowaways, but it says repotting isn't needed and suggests well-draining cactus mix, so the actual fix (a less draining soil) is only hinted at for non-succulents. It isn't clearly harmful because the repot is conditional and stowaway removal helps.
